newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's c/a deficit reinforces NZ$ overvalued -Cullen.
newsitem.headline: NZ's c/a deficit reinforces NZ$ overvalued -Cullen.

text.p: NZ opposition Labour Party finance spokesman Michael Cullen said on Friday international views the currency was seriously overvalued would be reinforced by the March current account deficit of 4.8 percent of GDP.

"A current account deficit of this size -- approaching five percent of GDP -- when the economy is supposedly at the bottom of a trough is going to send very bad signals to the international financial markets.
"Their judgement that the New Zealand dollar is seriously overvalued is going to be reinforced by these numbers," Cullen said in a statement.
He said the decline in the NZ dollar in the last two months would not be enough to reverse the current account position, or satisfy the markets an adequate correction had occurred.
Cullen said the coalition government should revisit the fundamentals of its economic policy, by moving to a directly export-led growth strategy.
"There is a need to restore confidence in the economy...in such a way that the emphasis shifts towards supporting the tradeables sector and ensuring that resources flow into that sector," he said.

"The signal the government is sending by its own activity, including the promised ($1 billion) tax cuts next year, is that investment should move in the opposite direction into the domestic, non-tradeable sector of the economy."
